tagline: The Army's old supply road, from Oklahoma to the fort gates.
intro: From the Oklahoma line the byway runs north on US 69 Alternate through Baxter Springs, then up US 69 by way of Pittsburg, Fort Scott and Pleasanton, around the Kansas City side on I-435, and on K-5 and K-7 into Leavenworth, ending at the gates of the fort after some 168 miles. It keeps to the line of the military road the Army used to move soldiers and supplies across eastern Kansas.

Baxter Springs began at a spring the Osage had long visited, on a hillside by that road, where a settler named Baxter kept a tavern on Cherokee land. Agents tried more than once to put him off it. He stayed until the land itself was opened to settlement.

moments.title: Fort Scott National Historic Site
moments.text: Built in 1842 without walls, since the open ground and the artillery made them unnecessary, its buildings stand around a parade ground beside five acres of restored tallgrass prairie.

moments.title: Mine Creek Battlefield State Historic Site
moments.text: On October 25, 1864, some 2,800 Union cavalry caught about 8,000 of Price's retreating Confederates stalled at the creek crossing, in the only major battle fought in Kansas.

moments.title: Fort Leavenworth
moments.text: The end of the road and the reason for it, an Army post since 1827 and the oldest permanent settlement in Kansas, where the 10th Cavalry's Buffalo Soldiers were formed in 1866.
